## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: NONE

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation approach:** I examined the full diff of the supplied "fix" commit (`0cc556e`), then used `git blame` on the immediate parent (`b05f577`) to find when each changed line was originally introduced, and inspected the parent commit `f58e557` (same author, same day, 19 minutes earlier) which had just added the `GitLabLogoutAction` class and the `setValue`/`extractToken` code paths it touches. I also checked the Jackson dependency version and class hierarchy (`com.fasterxml.jackson.core.JsonProcessingException extends IOException`) to verify whether the removed `catch` clause had any semantic effect.

**(2) What the "fix" commit actually changes:**
- `GitLabLogoutAction.getGitLabText()`: renames local variable `j` → `jenkins`, and removes an unused local `GitLabSecurityRealm glsr` cast that was never referenced in that branch (the branch only returns the literal string `"GitLab"`).
- `GitLabSecurityRealm.setValue()`: converts an `if/else-if` chain into an equivalent `switch` statement over the same `node.toLowerCase()` values, with identical branch bodies and the same `default`/`else` throwing `ConversionException`.
- `GitLabSecurityRealm.extractToken()`: removes a `catch (JsonProcessingException e)` block. Since `JsonProcessingException` is a subclass of `IOException` (confirmed via `com.fasterxml.jackson.core` in the imports, jackson 2.9.1 per `pom.xml`), and both catch blocks called the identical `Log.error(e.getMessage(), e)`, removing the more-specific catch has **no observable behavioral difference** — the subsequent `catch (IOException e)` handles it identically.

Every one of these three changes is behavior-preserving: a rename, dead-code removal, an equivalent control-flow restructuring, and removal of a redundant (not incorrect) exception handler. There is no logic change, no altered condition, no different return value, and no different exception handling outcome between the pre- and post-commit code.

**(3) Evidence supporting "no real bug fixed":**
- `git blame` shows the `setValue` if/else chain and the `extractToken` try/catch predate this "fix" by over a year (commits from `2016-04-15`, authored `a23fc724`/`984ad8c6`/`17189837`), yet no other commit in between touched or reported issues with this logic.
- The `GitLabLogoutAction.java` file itself was created by the *immediately preceding* commit `f58e557` (same author, ~19 minutes prior), meaning the "cleanup" in `0cc556e` is the same author immediately tidying up code they had just written — not a fix for a bug that existed in the codebase over time.
- No behavioral difference exists between the pre- and post-image of any hunk in `0cc556e`; I could not identify any input/output, exception-handling, or control-flow change.

Given there is no functional bug fixed by `0cc556e` — it is a pure refactor/cleanup — there is no corresponding bug-introducing commit to identify. I report this with high confidence based on the semantic equivalence shown above, though I note some residual uncertainty since I cannot fully rule out an extremely subtle behavioral difference (e.g., stack trace line numbers differing between the two catch blocks) that wouldn't register as a "bug" in the conventional sense anyway.
